question: An engineer must perform an initial configuration of VXLAN Tunnel End-Point functionality on the Cisco Nexus 9000 Series platform. All the necessary features are already enabled on the switch. Which configuration set must be used to accomplish this goal?
options: NX9K(config)# interface loopback0 NX9K(config-if)# ip address 10.10.10.11/32 NX9K(config)# interface VLAN10 NX9K(config-if)# ip unnumbered loopback0 NX9K(config)# interface nve1 NX9K(config-if-nve)# source-interface loopback0

NX9K(config)# interface loopback0 NX9K(config-if)# ip address 10.10.10.11/32 NX9K(config)# interface overlay0 NX9K(config-if-overlay)# source-interface loopback0 NX9K(config)# interface VLAN10 NX9K(config-if-nve)# source-interface loopback0

NX9K(config)# interface loopback0 NX9K(config-if)# ip address 10.10.10.11/32 NX9K(config)# interface tunnel1 NX9K(config-if)# tunnel source loopback0 NX9K(config)# interface ethernet1/1 NX9K(config-if)# ip unnumbered loopback0

NX9K(config)# interface loopback0 NX9K(config-if)# ip address 10.10.10.11/32 NX9K(config)# interface nve1 NX9K(config-if-nve)# source-interface loopback0 NX9K(config)# interface ethernet1/1 NX9K(config-if)# ip unnumbered loopback0
theory: A VTEP's identity on the underlay is a loopback interface with its own IP address, which is bound to the NVE interface via "source-interface loopback0" so that VXLAN encapsulation uses that loopback IP as the VTEP source/destination address. Physical uplinks used to reach that loopback across the underlay are typically configured as "ip unnumbered loopback0" to conserve address space on point-to-point links rather than assigning a separate subnet to every interface, which is why both the nve1 interface and the physical uplink reference the same loopback. (CCNP/CCIE DCCOR Official Cert Guide, Chapter 3 — VXLAN NVE Configuration)
